 What We’re Looking For 
 Oxford is looking for a Delivery Coordinator to own change orders for a delivery pod and to run CAT 1 engagements alongside the team. Delivery is organized into pods, three in the US and one in the EU, and engagements belong to the pod rather than to any one person. The Delivery Lead assigns work across the pod based on capacity and skill fit. As the Delivery Coordinator in your pod, you will process change orders for every engagement category, whether it is CAT 1, 2, or 3, and you will take on CAT 1 engagements assigned by the Delivery Lead from the pod’s shared book.
 Today, your engagement work is limited to CAT 1 because of experience, not as a permanent ceiling. This role is the clearest growth path into a Delivery Manager role, and you will build toward CAT 2 and CAT 3 readiness as experience and capacity allow. There is one Delivery Coordinator per pod. The role has no direct reports and reports to the Managing Director, Engagement Management.
 Remote | Non-Exempt | Reports to the Managing Director, Engagement Management 
 What You’ll Do: 
 Serve as the single point of ownership for change orders across the pod, processing them for every engagement in CAT 1, 2, and 3 regardless of who is working it.
 Take on CAT 1 engagement work assigned by the Delivery Lead and run it end to end, from kickoff and ongoing management through reporting and closeout.
 Communicate deliverable quality and timeliness against contract and client expectations on the CAT 1 engagements you work.
 Support kickoff logistics across the pod as needed.
 Track time, expenses, and budget consumption across the pod’s engagements.
 Coordinate consultant onboarding and offboarding across the pod.
 Coordinate engagement team training activities across the pod.
 Attend the daily standup and keep the Delivery Lead current on change order and CAT 1 status.
 Keep your engagements and all pod change orders current in Monday.com and documented to the OneNote standard.
 Participate in the Community of Practice.
 Build toward CAT 2 and CAT 3 readiness as experience and capacity allow.

 CAT 1 engagements are managed to the same standard as any other pod engagement.
 Pod-wide change orders are processed without becoming a bottleneck for Leads and Managers.
 There is a clear readiness signal for promotion into CAT 2 and CAT 3 scope or a Delivery Manager role.
 Worth Noting 
 Delivery Manager — the Manager works any category but doesn't carry pod-wide change order ownership 
 Delivery Lead — the Lead works any category plus pod mentoring and owns project assignment for the pod, with no change order ownership.

Patterson isn't just a place to work, it's a partner that cares about your success. 
 One of the distinguishing marks of our company is the talented people who embrace the people-first, always advancing, and results-driven culture. Professional growth abounds in this motivating environment. We value the diverse talents and experiences our employees bring to Patterson and believe that they build a stronger and successful organization. 
 Job Summary 
The Project Manager II drives efficiency and innovation by managing projects throughout all stages of the project lifecycle from initiation through closure. The Project Manager II independently leads medium-sized projects and may assist on large programs, ensuring alignment with strategic objectives. The types of projects may include, but not limited to: SaaS, SAP enhancements, warehouse management improvements, cybersecurity, infrastructure upgrades, and office mergers. The Project Manager II is responsible for the execution of standard project deliverables including: Project Charters, stakeholder analysis, project plans, timelines, budgets, risk/issue/decision trackers, status reports, and retrospectives. The Project Manager II ensures project outcomes align with original Project Charter scope, KPIs, budget and schedule. 
 Essential Functions 
 Prepare Project Charters, coordinate kick-off meetings, and align stakeholders on objectives, KPIs, and communication plans
 Facilitate agile planning through collaboration with Technical Product Owners to define sprint schedules and establish go-live timelines
 Develop and maintain detailed project plans with milestones and task assignments; monitor progress to ensure timely delivery
 Utilize established methodologies to produce RAID logs, stakeholder analyses, decision trackers, and risk mitigation plans
 Document and communicate budget estimates and actuals from internal and external sources to stakeholders
 Identify potential risks, escalate issues to leadership, and implement mitigation strategies with regular updates
 Deliver consistent project status updates via reports, presentations, and meetings across multiple channels
 Lead the creation and execution of cutover and hypercare plans to support successful implementation
 Conduct retrospectives, share lessons learned, and recommend process enhancements for future projects
 Engage with managers and cross-functional teams (EPMO, GDA) to share best practices, discuss dependencies, and support team goals
 Comply with Company and department policies and standards; performs other duties as assigned
 Minimum Requirements 
 Bachelor's Degree in Computer Science, Management Information Sciences, Mathematics, Engineering, Business Finance or equivalent education and/or experience 
 3 years of Project Management Experience 
 Experience using project management tools and methodologies 
 Skills and Abilities 
 Proven ability to develop successful collaborative working relationships with a variety of industries. 
 Ability to effectively communicate with business leaders and collaborate with cross-functional department representatives. 
 Ability to manage projects of any type (technical and non-technical/business) and projects with international components. 
 Proven success managing large projects (6-18 months in duration) with many cross-functional teams (Corporate Technologies/IT and business).
